tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: Stop overpaying for the easy stuff. Here's a two-minute demo of it running. Video

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: It's live. Pick Auto Efficient in the model picker, or turn it on here: kilo.codes/6ThU8gm Matching the model to the task is the biggest thing you can do about your AI bill. This does it per request.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: If it's not sure, it doesn't guess. When a routing decision isn't clear, it falls back to Balanced, which uses a capable paid model. So quality has a floor. Cheap models only get used where they hold up.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: There's a setting for how aggressive it gets. "Best accuracy per dollar" takes the cheapest model that clears the bar. "Best accuracy" takes the strongest one. Set it per project, depending on whether you care more about cost or output.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: It's session-aware, so it doesn't thrash. A router that swaps models every turn loses context and gives you inconsistent output. Auto Efficient stays on a model that's working and only switches when a cheaper one clearly fits. You get per-request routing without the model changing mid-thread.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: The rankings are public. They're on the Kilo Leaderboard. You can open it, find the cheapest model that does well on your kind of work, and select it yourself. Auto Efficient just does that lookup on every request instead of making you do it.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: It picks models based on KiloBench. KiloBench runs continuously against every model in the catalog, on tasks pulled from real Kilo usage. If it routes you to a cheaper model, that model already scored well enough on that kind of work.

tweets.creator: @kilocode
tweets.text: You're paying frontier prices to rename a variable! Auto Efficient routes each request to the cheapest model that can handle it. Rename a variable, you get a small model. Plan a migration, you get a big one. You don't switch anything. How it works 🧵
